title: Voikov to Stomoniakov, Nr 1883/1188/S, Moscow to Berlin, 1 June 1921 (NARA M316 roll 42, frame 1273)

plaintext.source: No decipherment in the file; Bristol reports none.

transcription.source: NARA M316 frame, RG 64 digital copy
transcription.notes: Sharp type; about 5 letters marked lost by the typist.

system.summary: A columnar transposition of Russian in Latin letters: frequencies are Russian with no substitution, and the recovered key gives Russian text. Q is the soft or hard sign; punctuation is spelled out.

prior_solution.where: GC&CS read other Soviet links in 1921 (Tiltman); HW 12 and RG 457 6707N not seen; no reading of this message found

conditions.human_role: Named the catalogue entry and asked to keep attacking the letter traffic.
tools: lang engine with a Russian corpus from ru.wikipedia

solution.what: Fetched the OCR of the M316 reels and found runs of 5-letter groups, then fetched the frame image.
The letter traffic to Stomoniakov (2,310 letters, OCR) has Russian letter frequencies with no substitution.
Transcribed the message from the image, 615 letters plus 5 lost.
Columnar widths 5-36 on OCR and first model: nothing clear at 120,000 steps, though width 24 alone beat its shuffled controls.
Width 24, 250,000 steps, 9 restarts, masked lost letters: readable Russian, -3.73; the restarts agree in rotations.
Set Q to the soft sign from desiatq and vosemq, and rebuilt the model.
Polished by moving columns within the row: -3.21.
Item-by-item reading into a coherent purchase list with its own punctuation words and prod sled ending.
Scanned English corpora and two George Wither texts for the key rank pattern: best 10/24, chance level.

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026), by hand, word by word, decryption.txt against reading.txt; sure words only, a letter corrected in a key rebuilt here a hole. The telegram is wholly cipher, so nothing was separated. 105 reading words: 63 read as decrypted, 42 holes (11 bracketed or [...], 5 lost-letter words, 26 slipped words). 0.987 -> 0.600; class read -> read in part. v10_relabel.py gives 0.88 because the slipped words are not marked in the reading, so the dry run does not reproduce the figure.

validation.notes: Transposition: letters are unchanged, so the token-key test does not apply; shuffled-letter controls are in the notes.

outcome.method_basis: The 24-column key came from annealing against a Russian model with no crib, and gives a coherent purchase list.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cipher words only (16 Nov 2026), sure words only, counted by hand from decryption.txt against reading.txt: the telegram is wholly cipher (the heading in clear is not in the reading); 105 reading words (the 'zpt', 'dvoetochie' and 'prod sled' words included), 63 read as the decryption gives them and 42 holes: 11 words with letters supplied in brackets or marked [...], 5 words with a lost letter (?) filled in, and 26 words whose decrypted letters differ from the reading (radio or copying slips emended in a key recovered here). Before 0.987, counted over letters (8 of 615 unread).
outcome.notes: Key source unknown. Several letters are radio or copying slips, emended in brackets.

texts.label: Nr 1883/1188/S, 1 June 1921

reading_review.note: Read by the model as sentences item by item; no independent reader yet.

texts.summary: A buying order to Stomoniakov in Berlin: hardware for the goods-exchange fund with the countryside, listed with sizes (iron, nails, shovels, rakes, forks, axes, saws, chisels). It ends "continuation follows". The goods-exchange subject fits the Politburo decision on Kopp's proposal of 16 April 1921, by subject only.
texts.note: 16 Nov 2026, cipher words only: 63 of 105 words read as the decryption stands (60.0%); 42 holes (11 supplied or unread, 5 lost letters filled, 26 slipped words emended in a rebuilt key); before 0.987, counted over letters. The reading holds the cipher only, so nothing was split. v10_relabel.py gives 0.88 (it counts the bracketed words and the [...] only; the slipped and lost-letter words are not marked in the reading), so its figure does not reproduce this count.

gaps.item: the 26 words whose decrypted letters differ from the reading, the 5 words with a lost letter filled in, the unread word after 'four' (chetyre shjima) and the unexplained 'ce'
gaps.detail: one 615-letter telegram in a key recovered here, no second copy of it to check the slipped letters against; the omitted prepositions are not in the cipher
